title: 3.3 · Our class survey (Collect, chart, claim)
name: Our class survey (Collect, chart, claim)
summary: Students collect real data from the whole class with a two-question survey on paper slips, enter the tallies in Data Detective's My Data, choose a chart and pick a claim. Before they finish, each pair asks another pair whether their claim is fair and writes down the answer and the reason. Pairs share one device.
iCan: collect answers from the whole class with tally marks
put the numbers in a chart and make a claim the data shows
ask another pair if our claim is fair and listen to the reason
materials: survey slips with the two provided questions (one slip per student per question)
doNow: Vote on the board with one tally mark: which pet do you like best, dog, cat, other or none?
plan: Explore: My Data with the Do Now tallies

warmup.why: two retrieval items from 3.2, one vocabulary item, one preview of today, one more from 3.2

do: Open Data Detective at My Data on the projector (Open game at this chapter). Count the Do Now tally marks with the class in fives and enter each number with the steppers; pick the labels from the list: dog, cat, other, none.
Choose the bar chart. Read the claims on the screen out loud and ask the question below.
say: Real data comes from real people. Collecting it well is half the job.
A fair claim says only what the chart shows, about the people we asked.
ask: Is the claim most kids in the world like dogs fair? What can we really say from our chart?
explore.afterAsk: Take answers until someone says we only asked our class. Pick the claim about our class and pin it. Then hand out the survey slips.
explore.bigIdea: Real data comes from real people, and a fair claim says only what the data shows.

play.goal: both survey questions charted and one claim checked by another pair
play.stretch: a claim that uses both charts
play.pairs: pairs hand out and collect the slips for 5 minutes, then share one device: the navigator reads the tally sheet out loud while the driver enters the numbers; swap for the second question at the chime
lookFors: tally marks miscounted: count them in fives
claims about everyone when only our class was asked
a pair skipping the is-our-claim-fair check because they are sure they are right
play.misconception: A survey of our class tells us about our class, not about everyone, and a claim is fair only when the chart shows it.
earlyFinishers: help a neighbor without touching their screen

discuss: Did everyone's chart say the same thing? Why not?
What did the other pair say about your claim? Did you change it?
showMe: Two pairs with different charts for the same question show them side by side on the projector; the class finds where the numbers differ and why.

exit.sentencePrompt: What is your pair's claim? Did another pair say it is fair? Write yes or no and their reason.
exit.frame: Our claim is ___; another pair said ___.

rubric.line: Collecting and charting: a chart that answers the question
levels: Collected answers or made a chart
Made a chart from the class tallies that answers the question
Also says why that chart shows the answer best

rubric.line: Claims: a claim the chart supports
levels: Writes a claim the chart shows, about the class
Also names the numbers that back it up

rubric.line: Feedback: asking another pair if the claim is fair
levels: Says another pair looked at the claim
Writes the other pair's answer and their reason
Also says what the pair kept or changed because of it

exit.paper: exit half-sheet (two per page) with the three items and the sentence frame

support: the two provided questions and a printed tally sheet with the categories filled in
count the tallies in fives with a finger on each group
claim tiles to pick from instead of writing one
stretch: a claim that uses both charts
a third question of the pair's own, with three categories and an other

unpluggedTwin.title: Tally and Grid
steps: Pairs hand out the two survey questions on slips and collect them.
They tally the answers on the tally sheet, counting in fives.
They color one square per answer on grid paper to make a bar chart, with labels.
They write a claim under the chart, then swap with another pair, who writes yes or no and one reason.
Share: hang the charts in a row. Which claims did the other pairs say were fair?

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: vote with one tally mark on the board for a favorite pet: dog, cat, other or none

Survey on paper, 25 minutes: pairs hand out the two survey questions on slips, tally the answers, color a bar chart on grid paper and write a claim; then they ask another pair if the claim is fair and write the answer. If devices are out, Data Detective, chapter My Data, quest code 7 1 2 0, takes the tallies; playing signed out is fine.
Paper exit ticket: the half-sheet with three questions and the sentence frame. Collect it.

shortPeriod40.discuss: Did everyone's chart say the same thing? Why not?
shortPeriod40.keep: the exit ticket is never cut

add: the third question stretch after Play
the Tally and Grid twin as a paper copy to hang in the room
10 minutes of the Unit 3 review on Brain Board

notes: No names on the slips: the survey counts answers, not people.
No no-right-answer poll exists in the live sets yet, so the survey runs on paper slips.
The fairness check is the question step evidence: one yes or no and one reason from another pair.
Shared devices: this is an odd lesson in the unit, so partner A signs in; the gradebook and the Standards tab count the signed-in student.

Big idea: Real data comes from real people, and a fair claim says only what the data shows.

We will talk about:

steps.title: Warm-up (live)
steps.body: Five quick questions. Your teacher shows them on the projector or starts them live.

steps.title: Play: My Data
steps.body:
Goal: both survey questions charted and one claim checked by another pair. Stretch: write one claim that uses both charts.
If the game asks for a quest code, it is 7 1 2 0.
Pairs: hand out the slips, collect them and tally them. The navigator reads the tally sheet; the driver enters the numbers. Swap for the second question. Before you finish, ask another pair: is our claim fair? Write their answer and their reason.

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.body: Three quick questions about surveys and fair claims.
